subject: Onramp options and sizing worksheet for LatticeBio
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@latticebio.ai>

Cc: Diego Ruiz <diego@latticebio.ai>
Date: 2026-09-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Onramp planning: dedicated capacity request

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency profile. We're starting procurement planning for the inference platform that will run our protein-folding inference pipeline in Q4. High-level ask: can you send a compact worksheet with 2–3 dedicated capacity options (cluster footprint, minimum GPUs, expected ramp schedule and common activation windows) so we can evaluate budget vs. risk?

A few quick notes on our workload:
- Peak inference concurrency: ~220 req/s (95th percentile) across 8 model variants.
- Typical sequence lengths: 1K tokens avg, with spikes to 4K for some experiments.
- Latency target (P95): <250ms for production endpoints.
- Traffic profile: baseline steady-state during working hours (M–F 6am–8pm PT), with two experimental bursts per month that double traffic for 12–36 hours.

I'm attaching our forecast and a short model profile to help sizing. Procurement timeline: we need an internal decision by end of September; draft SOW/quote would be helpful this week if possible.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through numbers.

Best,
Elena Torres
Head of ML Infrastructure
LatticeBio
Attachments: LatticeProd-traffic-forecast.csv (csv), model_profile_summary.jsonl (jsonl)
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@latticebio.ai>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>, Diego Ruiz <diego@latticebio.ai>
Date: 2026-09-12T13:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onramp planning: dedicated capacity request

Hi Elena — thanks for the details and the attachments, those are perfect. I sketched an "onramp worksheet" below with three pragmatic paths so your procurement and infra leads can compare trade-offs. I've cc'd Mateo and Lukas for technical confirmation and to flag any constraints.

Quick summary (ballpark):

Option A — Conservative Baseline (lower spend, modest risk)
- Baseline: 8 x vA100-equivalent GPUs (steady-state)
- Minimum active guarantee: 8 GPUs (no cold-start)
- Burst mechanism: 2x burst credits for 48-hour experiments (adds temporary capacity up to 16 GPUs)
- Ramp plan: 2 weeks to full baseline after contract start (warm-up + prewarming windows)
- Pros/cons: Lower monthly commit, higher risk on sustained spikes >2x

Option B — Staged Floor (balanced availability)
- Baseline: 12 x vA100-equivalent GPUs
- Minimum active guarantee: 6 GPUs (keeps core latency-critical lanes warm)
- Burst mechanism: automated scaling to 24 GPUs during bursts (with pre-booked burst blocks)
- Ramp plan: 6-week phased activation: Week 0-2 provisioning + prewarming, Week 3-6 gradual traffic shift from hosted to dedicated
- Pros/cons: Good latency headroom and predictable cost profile; recommended for most experimental production workloads

Option C — High-availability Ladder (lowest risk)
- Baseline: 20 x vA100-equivalent GPUs
- Minimum active guarantee: 12 GPUs
- Burst mechanism: guaranteed spare capacity + geo-fallback routing for Global DR tests
- Ramp plan: 8–10 week activation with canary traffic and A/B routing
- Pros/cons: Best for low-latency SLAs and frequent heavy experiments; higher monthly commitment

Notes and assumptions:
- We converted your forecast to vA100-equivalent figures using your average seq lengths and token rates; final kernel/quantization tuning can move these numbers by ~10–25%.
- "vA100-equivalent" is Redwood's internal sizing unit (same as used in our contract tables).
- Burst credits are billed differently from baseline commit; we can model blended unit economics in the quote.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Quick alignment call with Mateo and Lukas to validate latency P95 targets and concurrency assumptions (30 min).
2) We produce a one-page SOW + line-item cost sheet for the option you prefer (we can include both baseline + detailed burst costing).
3) If procurement needs it, we can add a 60-day onramp with trial credits to reduce purchasing risk.

Would you like us to draft Option B as a starting proposal? If yes, I'll have a draft quote + SOW by EOD next business day.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-13T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onramp planning: dedicated capacity request

Thanks for looping me in. I ran a quick back-of-envelope using Elena's traffic.csv and the model summary; here are concrete technical clarifications and a recommended activation schedule to hit P95 <250ms.

Technical sizing notes:
- With 1K avg / 4K spike sequences we expect ~18–22 tokens/sec per vA100-equivalent core for your quantization profile; that maps to the baseline numbers Avery listed.
- The key leverage is KV-cache warmup — we recommend a 48–72 hour prewarm window before shifting live traffic for each major model variant.
- For the monthly double-traffic bursts, materializing a preprovisioned 48-hour burst block (booked ahead) reduces cold-run latency and avoids throttling.

Refined recommended plan (tied to Option B):
- Day 0–14: Provision 6 GPUs and run internal warmup + synthetic traffic; keep hosted fallback for 25% of traffic.
- Week 3–4: Increase to 12 GPUs; begin incremental traffic cutover for low-risk endpoints.
- Week 5–6: Reach full baseline 12 GPUs handling 85–100% of traffic; enable burst-booked blocks (16–24 GPUs available on demand).
- Minimum live guarantee we will recommend in the SOW: 6 GPUs (to keep steady-state latencies under target even if burst credits are exhausted).

Attachment: I attached a small workbook with compute-hour estimates and a simple cost model (redwood-scaling-estimate.xlsx).

Operational suggestions:
- Add a 30-day rollback clause in the activation window to lower purchasing risk.
- Recommend a weekly warmup job during the first 8 weeks to keep caches healthy.

I'll sync with Lukas on the kernel and quantization knobs for the formal quote. Happy to jump on the alignment call tomorrow morning.

—Mateo
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-scaling-estimate.xlsx (xlsx)
